body_markdown:
Following the example of the mid-size Tacoma pickup and the body-on-frame Sequoia SUV, the 2027 Tundra half-ton is the latest Toyota to gain a more accessible off-road package aimed at overlanding. Of course,[you already knew this](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/toyota-adds-trailhunter-packages-to-2027-tundra-and-sequoia/) : What you didn’t know until now were all the details and, most importantly, the price.


The 2027 Tundra starts at $45,085 (SR), representing a $1630 jump over the 2026 model. The hybrid TRD Pro model costs $77,595, occupying an appropriately lofty place in the Tundra hierarchy; after all, Toyota bills this as “the ultimate off-road expression of the Tundra.” (We would have expected it to say something like, “Heck yeah, dirt!”, but what do we know.) The TRD Pro model is distinguished by newly designed Fox shocks—the three-mode QS3 model, to be specific, currently offered by the supplier for motorcycles and snowmobiles and adjustable (sans tools) to three modes: soft, medium, and firm. Of course, TRD Pro buyers also enjoy an exclusive color. This year’s is Honeycomb, an earth tone that replaces the very water-toned Wave Runner from 2026. As all your fellow drivers will love to hear, the lumen output of the light bar and fog lights has increased for 2027.

Both the TRD Pro trim and the Trailhunter package bring 4WD, a locking rear differential, skid plates, Crawl Control (think cruise control but for low-speed off-road maneuvers), and Multi-Terrain Select. The Trailhunter package ($5880) uses a different suspension system from Old Man Emu, most likely tuned for heavier loads and slower off-road shenanigans than the TRD Pro’s setup is designed to handle. The Trailhunter package is based on the SR5 trim—specifically, a non-hybrid, 4WD CrewMax model with the 5.5-foot bed—for a total of $60,225.


Toyota | Benjamin Hutton


Like its SUV sibling the Sequoia, the 2027 Tundra also receives various technology and convenience upgrades. The 14-inch infotainment screen is now standard, replacing the 8-inch model on lower trims; Proactive Driving Assist has been added to the suite of safety features; and Drive Recorder Dash Cam, which recruits the exterior cameras to record 20-second snippets of video either on-demand or automatically and plays them on the central display. Another cool feature the ’27 Tundra shares with the Sequoia is a 2.4-kW inverter for your off-the-grid power needs.


The V-6-based gas-only and hybrid powertrains carry over to 2027, with one exception: The 4×2 version of the hybrid truck has been dropped.

We’re headed to Texas to drive the 2027 Tundra next week, where we’ll report on more of the nitty-gritty details of the updated truck, like the new steering wheel (all trims except the SR get a heated wheel standard, yay!) and the “new premium Adaptive Variable Suspension and Air Suspension combination” available across all trims. Any questions you’d like us to ask the people who made the truck? Let us know in the comments below!
